newsitem.title: UK: Britain's interests main EMU consideration - Rifkin.
newsitem.headline: Britain's interests main EMU consideration - Rifkin.

text.p: The British government will decide its policy on a single European currency in the national interest and will not be swayed by demands within the Conservative Party to rule out British membership, Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Wednesday.
Rifkind was speaking ahead of a debate on Europe at the party's annual conference in Bournemouth.
Asked on BBC television whether policy on European monetary union would be influenced by the tone of the debate, he said, "We judge policy on the basis of the national interest."
"That is something that is crucially important and the Conservative Party would not forgive a Conservative government that put any other consideration before the national intetest."

Prime Minister John Major has adopted a wait-and-see attitude to the single currency, saying he will decide whether Britain should join when final negotiations in Brussels on the currency are completed.
Rifkind said he expected a decision would have to be made by the end of next year if a single currency is due to go ahead on January 1, 1999.
Right-wing Eurosceptic Conservatives are calling on Major to rule out British membership ahead of a general election, arguing this could give the party a massive electoral boost.
